raw_response:
*Sits on the edge of the kang, lights a cigarette, looks at the calendar on the wall*

Alright, 14 mu. Not much, but it's what my father left me and I've worked it all my life. My eldest is in town — construction, when there's work. My wife and me do most of it here. Daughter-in-law comes out for cotton picking. Grandson's still in school, can't put him in the field.

Here's how I'm thinking about it this year:

**The wheat** — I put it in last October like always. About 8 mu, the two plots closer to the house because they get the irrigation easier. It's up now, looking alright. Not as thick as I'd like in the low spot — it was dry when I sowed. Used my own seed from last year's crop, like I always do. Bought the cheap compound stuff at planting, 2 bags for those 8 mu. When spring gets going I'll top-dress one bag of urea before the irrigation. Neighbor Old Liu says to do it twice but I can't afford two and I never have. My wheat does fine, 700-800 jin a mu in a good year. I'll water it maybe three times — once now when it greens up, once at jointing, once when it's heading. Water from the well costs money so I don't waste it. If the sky gives rain I skip one.

**The maize** — comes right after the wheat in June. Same 8 mu. That turnaround is always a rush, two, three days to cut the wheat, burn the stubble a little, and get the maize in. I buy hybrid seed, the Zhengdan number, because you can't save maize seed, it won't come up right. Son brings a bag from the supply shop in the town. Fertilizer — one bag of compound at planting, and one bag of urea when it's about knee-high. If July is dry I'll water once, maybe twice. Maize doesn't need as much water as the wheat but if it's dry at tasseling you lose everything.

**The cotton** — 6 mu, the strip along the road. It's what gives us the cash. I've done cotton all my life, hands know the work better than my head does. I plant end of April when the ground warms up. Use mulch film, everybody does now. Fertilizer I put mostly before planting, about 2 bags compound, maybe a little urea later when it's flowering if it looks weak. Cotton is the one that eats pesticide — the worms come, the aphids come, sometimes you spray four, five times. Cost adds up. Last year the price was low, didn't make much. This year if prices stay bad I don't know, but I can't switch now, I already bought the seed.

**Money worry** — the government pays a little for grain but cotton is what keeps cash in the house. I try not to borrow. If I spend everything on fertilizer and then the drought comes or the price drops, we got no cushion. So I don't put down the full amount the extension fellow talks about. I put what I know works.

**Labor** — my wife and me can handle most of it. For cotton picking we'll need the daughter-in-law and maybe pay a neighbor's wife some days. Wheat harvest and maize planting we hire the combine, everybody does, 50 yuan a mu for the combine, no way around it.
